incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $F$-algebra with centre $Z(A):=\{z\in A:za=az	ext{ for all }a\in A\}$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). A **central idempotent** of $A$ is an idempotent $e\in Z(A)$; it is **primitive** when $e\ne0$ and $e$ is not the sum of two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents. Then $Z(A)$ is a finite-dimensional commutative $F$-algebra, so $1\in Z(A)$ admits a decomposition $$1=e_1+\cdots+e_k$$ into pairwise orthogonal primitive central idempotents ([[lem-the-identity-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-decomposes-into-primitive-central-idempotents]]), and this decomposition is unique up to order ([[lem-central-idempotent-decompositions-of-one-are-unique]]). A **block** of $A$ is the two-sided ideal $B=eA=Ae$ cut out by a primitive central idempotent $e$. The blocks are pairwise orthogonal two-sided ideals, $A=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_k$ as $F$-algebras with units $e_i$, each $B_i$ is an indecomposable two-sided ideal, and for every (not necessarily finite-dimensional) $A$-module $M$ one has $M=\bigoplus_{i=1}^ke_iM$ as $A$-modules; a simple $A$-module $S$ satisfies $e_iS\ne0$ for exactly one $i$ and then $S=e_iS$ lies in the corresponding block. Nothing here asserts that a block is semisimple or simple, and the construction is choice-free.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$ and $A$ a unital $R$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) which is free as an $R$-module on a finite set $C=\{c^{\lambda}_{st}:\lambda\in\Lambda,\ s,t\in T(\lambda)\}$, where $(\Lambda,\unrhd)$ is a finite poset ([[def-partial-order]]; its strict order is written $\rhd$) and each $T(\lambda)$ is a finite set. For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $A^{\rhd\lambda}$ be the $R$-submodule of $A$ spanned by all $c^{\mu}_{uv}$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$. Then $(C,\Lambda)$ is a **cellular basis** of $A$, and $A$ is a **cellular algebra**, if: (i) the $R$-linear map $i:A\to A$ with $i(c^{\lambda}_{st})=c^{\lambda}_{ts}$ for all $\lambda,s,t$ is an algebra anti-automorphism of $A$, i.e. $i(ab)=i(b)i(a)$ and $i(1)=1$ (equivalently $i$ is an isomorphism of $A$ with the opposite algebra; the displayed formula forces $i^2=\mathrm{id}$); and (ii) for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, every $t\in T(\lambda)$ and every $a\in A$ there exist $r_v\in R$ ($v\in T(\lambda)$) with $$c^{\lambda}_{st}\,a\equiv\sum_{v\in T(\lambda)}r_v\,c^{\lambda}_{sv}\pmod{A^{\rhd\lambda}}.$$

**Cell modules.** For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $C^{\lambda}$ be the free $R$-module with basis $\{c^{\lambda}_t:=c^{\lambda}_{tt}:t\in T(\lambda)\}$; condition (ii) makes $C^{\lambda}$ a right $A$-module by $c^{\lambda}_t a:=\sum_v r_vc^{\lambda}_v$ when $c^{\lambda}_{tt}a\equiv\sum_v r_vc^{\lambda}_{tv}\pmod{A^{\rhd\lambda}}$, and it makes $C^{\lambda}$ a left $A$-module via $i$. The module $C^{\lambda}$ is the **(right) cell module** of $\lambda$, and $A^{\unrhd\lambda}/A^{\rhd\lambda}\cong C^{\lambda}\otimes_R C^{\lambda}$ via $c^{\lambda}_{st}+A^{\rhd\lambda}\mapsto c^{\lambda}_s\otimes c^{\lambda}_t$. A cellular algebra may have several cellular bases.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ with standard basis $\{T_w\}$ and star anti-automorphism $*$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], [[lem-the-star-antiautomorphism-of-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). For a composition (in particular a partition) $\mu$ of $n$ put $m_\mu:=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w\in H$, the **row symmetrizer** of the standard Young subgroup $S_\mu$ ([[def-young-subgroup-tabloid-and-permutation-module]]); the sum has $|S_\mu|=\prod_i\mu_i!$ terms. For a row-standard $\mu$-tableau $s$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) let $d(s)\in S_n$ be the unique permutation of minimal length with $s=t^{\mu}d(s)$, where $t^{\mu}$ is the row-standard tableau obtained by entering $1,2,\dots,n$ in increasing order from left to right along the rows; $d(s)$ is the distinguished right-coset representative of $S_\mu$ in $S_n$ and $S_\mu$ is the stabiliser of $t^\mu$ ([[def-row-and-column-stabilizers-of-a-tableau]]). For row-standard $\mu$-tableaux $s,t$ define the **Murphy element** $$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}\,m_{\mu}\,T_{d(t)}\in H,$$ and for a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ shorten $m_t:=m_{tt}=T_{d(t)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$. Then $m_{st}^{*}=m_{ts}$ for all row-standard $s,t$ of the same shape, and $m_\mu T_w=q^{\ell(w)}m_\mu$ for every $w\in S_\mu$.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let $L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements ([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$, every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist $a_v\in R$ with $$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$ where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard $\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values. Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in $L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.

incoming_contract_bindings.literal_statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Let $\Lambda$ be the set of partitions of $n$ ordered by dominance $\unrhd$ ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]), and for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $T(\lambda)=\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ be the set of standard $\lambda$-tableaux ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). Then the **Murphy basis theorem** holds: the family $$\mathcal M=\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$$ is an $R$-basis of $H$, and $(\mathcal M,\Lambda)$ is a cellular basis of $H$ in the sense of [[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]. Explicitly: (i) $m_{st}^{*}=m_{ts}$ for all $\lambda$ and $s,t$; and (ii) for every $\lambda$, every $t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ and every $h\in H$ there exist $r_v\in R$ with $$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{\rhd\lambda}},$$ where $H^{\rhd\lambda}$ is spanned by the $m_{uv}$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$. The theorem holds over every commutative coefficient ring with $q\in R^{\times}$ and assumes no semisimplicity; the total number of Murphy elements is $\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}|\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)|^2=n!$ ([[cor-sum-of-squares-of-standard-tableau-numbers]]), matching the rank of $H$.
